instructions:
### ROLE ###
You maintain a small, growing set of CONCEPT SCHEMES (entity categories) for a knowledge registry built from cybersecurity incident reports. A group of entities extracted from several reports has just been found to be close to each other and far from every existing scheme. Decide whether the group is a genuinely new scheme or an alias of an existing one, and name it.

### EXISTING SCHEMES ###
- Email Address: An electronic mail address used for communication, contact, or observed in cyber threat activity.
- Domain Name: An internet domain name or subdomain used for network communication, hosting services, or cyber threat infrastructure.
- IP Address: A numerical label assigned to a device connected to a computer network, used for routing, hosting, or threat infrastructure.
- Country: A sovereign state or recognized nation involved as a threat origin, target location, or geopolitical context in cyber incident reporting.
- Malware Family: A distinct family, variant, or strain of malicious software designed to disrupt, compromise, or extract data from computer systems.
- Threat Actor: An individual, group, or organization responsible for initiating or conducting malicious cyber operations.
- Malicious File: A computer file, document, or script used, delivered, or generated as part of malicious cyber activity.
- Vulnerability: A security flaw or weakness in software, hardware, or system components that can be exploited by threat actors.

### THE GROUP ###
Each line is one entity with the description written at extraction time:
- MISP [software product] — An open-source threat intelligence platform used for sharing and analyzing cyber threat data.
- PowerShell [software product] — A task automation and configuration management framework developed by Microsoft.
- MS Office Word [software product] — A widely used word processing application developed by Microsoft.

### RULES ###
- A scheme is a KIND of entity (e.g. "Hacker group", "Malware family", "Software product", "Government body", "Internet domain", "Country"), never a role in an incident and never a single entity.
- Return `"verdict": "alias-of"` with `"target"` set to an existing scheme's label when the group is the same kind as that scheme (different wording, same meaning). Judge by MEANING of the descriptions, not by surface words.
- Return `"verdict": "new"` when no existing scheme covers the group. Then give:
  - `prefLabel`: a short English noun phrase, 1–3 words, singular, Title Case (e.g. "Malware Family").
  - `definition`: one sentence, at most 25 words, stating what belongs to the scheme, general enough to hold across reports.
  - `altLabels`: 0–3 alternative English labels.
- If the group mixes clearly different kinds, name the kind of the MAJORITY and list the minority entity names in `outliers`.
- If uncertain between alias and new, prefer `new`: an extra scheme can be merged later; a wrong merge cannot be undone cheaply.

### OUTPUT ###
A single raw JSON object, no markdown fences, no commentary:
{ "verdict": "new" | "alias-of", "target": "<existing label or null>", "prefLabel": "...", "definition": "...", "altLabels": [...], "outliers": [...] }
text: Decide and name the group now.
response: {"verdict": "new", "target": null, "prefLabel": "Software Product", "definition": "A computer program, application, or software platform used for operational, administrative, security, or general computing purposes.", "altLabels": ["Software", "Software Application", "Software Tool"], "outliers": []}
